vignette: Kai'a had always been a man who cherished his quiet moments, but after the cyclone ravaged his small island community, those moments became laced with danger. The howling winds and torrential rains that night still echoed in his mind, making it hard for him to shake off the feeling of helplessness that lingered long after the storm had passed. His wife, Leilani, had been taken from him in the chaos, leaving Kai'a alone to pick up the pieces. As an auditor, Kai'a's work required him to visit various locations, but he found himself increasingly avoiding unfamiliar places, fearing he couldn't assess the danger lurking within. The silence of these new environments unnerved him; unusual quiet made him feel like something ominous was about to unfold. Even delays in his daily routine would send his mind racing, assuming the worst had happened. Kai'a tried to cope by smoking more, a habit he'd kicked years ago but now found himself reverting to when anxiety crept in. He also avoided relaxing, fearing that letting his guard down would leave him vulnerable to the dangers he was convinced were lurking everywhere. Talking about the cyclone or its aftermath with others only seemed to make things worse, so he kept those conversations locked away. The memories of that night still haunted Kai'a. The smell of saltwater and debris wafting through his nostrils could transport him back to the moment the storm surge hit their small coastal town. He'd taste the metallic tang of fear on his tongue, just as he had when Leilani was taken from him. Yet, despite the vividness of these recollections, Kai'a sometimes struggled to believe that what happened had actually occurred. The event felt surreal, like a nightmare from which he couldn't wake up. When Kai'a allowed himself moments of happiness or relaxation, it was as if his brain would immediately counter with reminders of the dangers waiting around every corner. Feeling happy made him feel exposed and vulnerable all over again. Spatial triggers, such as walking through physical locations that reminded him of his island home, could evoke an overwhelming sense of unease. The darkness at night became a special torment for Kai'a. Waking up in the dark would send his heart racing, as if he was right back in the midst of the cyclone's fury. His mind told him that happiness and relaxation were luxuries he couldn't afford, that he needed to remain vigilant against an uncertain world. Kai'a had come to believe that the world was a treacherous place, full of hidden dangers waiting to pounce on the unwary. He felt emotionally numb, as if he'd been living in a state of suspended animation since Leilani's passing. Avoiding unfamiliar places and silences only served to reinforce this worldview. It was this cycle of fear and avoidance that finally drove Kai'a to seek help. He knew he couldn't keep going on like this - the loneliness and anxiety eating away at him, the memories refusing to be silenced. What frightened him most was losing himself completely in the aftermath of the cyclone, becoming a shadow of the man he once was. With each passing day, Kai'a felt his grip on reality tenuous at best. He yearned for peace, for a chance to lay down his burdens and remember what it meant to live without fear. But until that day came, he'd continue to struggle against the memories, triggers, and dangers that haunted him every step of the way.
